correction_note: An earlier version of this file (committed as bc5da27) claimed chain_check_results.json was stale/non-reproducible. That claim was a FALSE POSITIVE caused by my own test methodology: in the first clean-clone run I re-ran D-tda/02_mv_resolution.py a second time (to capture N=8 timing) AFTER D-tda/04_kunneth_scan_results.py had already run. 02_mv_resolution.py and 04_kunneth_scan_results.py both write exports.json, with different hardcoded 'status' text (02_mv_resolution.py:160 says '...depends on declared inputs (local model of a resolved point)'; 04_kunneth_scan_results.py:109 says '...depends on declared input resolution_local_model (tier L)'), and 02_mv_resolution.py's partial write (immediately after its first requested N finishes) silently overwrote 04's canonical export with no error. Diffing THAT corrupted clone state against the committed file produced the apparent one-line mismatch. A second, disciplined clean-clone run (fresh clone, single pass, 00->01->02->03->04 in order, no re-runs) reproduced D-tda/exports.json, D-tda/results.json AND chain/chain_check_results.json byte-for-byte identical to the committed files. git log -p on D-tda/exports.json and on 04_kunneth_scan_results.py confirms the committed 'resolution_local_model (tier L)' wording has been there since the single commit that ever touched either file (d5f8301); there was never a different committed version. Chain track passes cleanly. The retracted claim is removed from violations/reruns below and replaced with the narrower, still-real finding: the two scripts sharing one output path with no order-guard is a genuine latent fragility (demonstrated: an out-of-order re-run silently corrupts the shared file with exit 0 and no warning) even though the actual committed pipeline, run once in the natural order, is fully reproducible.

violations: audit/k3t2_rigidity_v3/C-lattices/results.json rigidity entry for parameter_inserted='chi_top' is labelled RIGID_GIVEN_DEFINITION, but its own fields read: solution_set='chi_top=24 unique given the declared inputs (it is a computation, not a scan)', negative_control='none realizable... not a control; labelled HYPOTHETICAL and not counted', control_perturbs_same_parameter=false. Ground rule 8 defines RIGID_GIVEN_DEFINITION as 'RIGID once named defining inputs are granted', and RIGID itself requires 'a structural selecting condition ... and a neighbouring value demonstrably fails'. This entry admits there is no scan, no selecting condition over candidate values, and no realizable negative control -- by its own words it is a straight-line formula evaluation (chi(O)=h0-h1+h2, then x12 via Noether), not a selection process at all. It therefore does not meet ANY of the rule-8 categories that require a demonstrated failure mode. The correct label is CONDITIONAL_ON_INPUT (a value fixed once the K3 definition -- K=O, b1=0 -- is granted, with no rigidity test performed), matching the label already correctly used two entries later in the SAME results.json for the 'typed Gram 3U+2(-E8)' entry, which is honestly self-labelled CONDITIONAL_ON_INPUT with selecting_condition='none (typed)'. audit/k3t2_rigidity_v3/B-dyons/results.json entry id='B5_margin' (script theta_margin_check.py) declares shared_inputs=['Jacobi_theta_definitions'] only. Reading theta_margin_check.py directly (its main block) shows it calls `knorm = Fr(load_inputs()['K3_elliptic_genus_factor_k']['value'])` and then `P2.compute(q1, QCHK-1, knorm, ...)` and `P3.run(q1, QCHK, 20, 60, knorm, Hh, ...)` where Hh is loaded from hurwitz_results.json. So B5's own computation depends on K3_elliptic_genus_factor_k (the declared k), on Hurwitz_H0/Kronecker_Hurwitz_relation (via the Hurwitz table it reads), on immortal_ansatz_form (via part3's ansatz), and on weak_Jacobi_ring_monomials (via part2's basis) -- none of which appear in B5's declared shared_inputs. Rule 7 requires 'every result lists shared_inputs: the names of the declared inputs it depends on', and this propagation is incomplete. Severity: LOW-MEDIUM -- B5 is a stability/margin cross-check (QMAX 40 vs 60 agreement), not itself a headline numeric claim, but a reader trusting the shared_inputs field to audit dependency propagation (as rule 7 intends) would be misled into thinking this check is nearly input-free.
